chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Minhāl, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A scorpion is taken out of the well dead?” He said: “Draw out ten buckets.” He said: I said: “And other than it from among carcasses?” He said: “All carcasses are alike, except a carcass that has become putrid. So if it is a carcass that has become putrid, then draw from it one hundred buckets; and if the smell overcomes it after one hundred buckets, then drain it all out.”
So the appropriate understanding concerning this report as well is that it indicates a kind of recommendation, not obligation.

key_terms.الرِّيحُ: the odor or smell that remains in the well
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed
key_terms.الْجِيَفُ: dead carcasses that fall into the water
key_terms.الْعَقْرَبُ: a scorpion found dead in the well
key_terms.مِائَةَ دَلْوٍ: the amount of one hundred buckets to be drawn out

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dead scorpion or carcass is found in a well according to al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on water in a well when a dead scorpion or other carcass is found in it, specifying how much water should be drawn out. It also distinguishes between an ordinary carcass and one that has become putrid, while the closing statement clarifies that this instruction is understood as recommendation rather than obligation.
